bottom_line: CA0579700 should use the official UC Davis Campus Boundary layer as the production custom footprint. The correct object is the discontiguous UC Davis campus-property footprint in and around Davis plus the Sacramento campus polygons, not Davis city, Yolo County, Sacramento County, Solano County, the whole UC Davis institution, or the Clery report's one-mile off-campus arrest halo.

official_scope_support.summary: The 2025 UC Davis Annual Security and Fire Safety Report says UC Davis Police patrol the Davis and UCD Health campuses, have primary jurisdiction over university-owned or operated property on and around those campuses, and separately notes that one-mile Davis-campus arrest authority should not be confused with the campus footprint.

official_map_support.summary: UC Davis publishes an official campus-boundary GIS layer with named Davis and Sacramento campus polygons, and the official maps-and-directions page links both the Sacramento campus map PDF and the Davis campus map.

explicit_exclusions: whole UC Davis institutional system proxy
California campus-police peace-officer authority as a blanket service-area geometry
the Clery report's one-mile Davis-campus halo as a substitute for mapped campus property

campus_boundary_layer.interpretation: The official UC Davis Campus Boundary layer is already a discontiguous campus-property footprint rather than a city or county polygon. It includes named Davis-side campus components plus three Sacramento Campus polygons, and its geographic extent stays confined to the Davis/Solano edge and Sacramento UC Davis Health corridor rather than statewide UC Davis holdings.

key_points: UC Davis Police patrol the Davis and UCD Health campuses 24/7.
The report says the department has primary jurisdiction over university-owned or operated property on and around the Davis and UCD Health campuses.
The same report separately describes one-mile Davis-campus arrest authority, which confirms that broader statutory authority should not be used as the footprint geometry.
The report identifies ANOVA Aggie Square as located on the UCD Health campus and within UC Davis Police law-enforcement jurisdiction.

sacramento_campus_property_crosscheck.summary: The official UC Davis Health maps page treats Sacramento as a distinct UC Davis campus, and the Aggie Square CEQA findings say Aggie Square is part of the UC Davis Sacramento Campus education/research/housing land-use framework connected to the hospital campus. That supports keeping the Sacramento-side boundary as a multipolygon campus footprint rather than collapsing to the main medical-center block only.

build_method.seed_geometry: Union all 10 official UC Davis Campus Boundary polygons from the public MapServer layer without buffering or manual expansion.
why_this_is_defensible: The layer is published by UC Davis as an explicit campus-boundary dataset and already encodes the discontiguous Davis and Sacramento campus-property structure that the doctrine calls for.

The 2025 Clery report and UC Davis Health map materials confirm that UCD Police serve the Davis and UCD Health campuses, while also warning against substituting broader off-campus arrest authority for the actual campus footprint.
The footprint naturally spans Yolo, Solano, and Sacramento counties, which is exactly why place or county proxying is misleading in this case.
omissions_by_design: No generic Davis, Yolo, Sacramento, or Solano proxy areas are included.
No one-mile off-campus halo is added around the Davis campus.
No remote UC Davis institutional sites outside the official Davis/Sacramento campus-boundary layer are included.

qa_notes: Rounded CSV shares sum to exactly 1.0 at 14 decimal places.
The official footprint intersects only 10 California block groups, making manual QA tractable.
The Davis-side official polygons cross the Yolo/Solano line, so a single-county localization would mechanically misallocate large shares.
The Sacramento-side acreage from the official campus-boundary layer is about 146.2 acres, matching the three Sacramento Campus polygons carried into the final union.

residual_caveats: The official campus-boundary service is the best public geometry source in this packet, but it is a campus-planning/property footprint rather than a separately published police beat file.

The packet intentionally does not add every possible Clery noncampus property or every location where UC Davis Police could exercise peace-officer authority; it stays with the mapped Davis/Sacramento campus-property footprint documented by UC Davis.

One small Sacramento polygon south along Stockton Boulevard is interpreted as part of the directly associated Sacramento-campus property set; that inclusion is supported by the official multipolygon campus-boundary layer and Aggie Square planning materials rather than by a separate parcel-by-parcel public boundary file.
